page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.48xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs built on the 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton architecture with Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.7 GHz. The system provides 768.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The processor implements 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware cryptographic acceleration including AES support. There are no onboard GPUs and no bundled local instance storage, requiring workloads to rely exclusively on remote EBS storage.

The instance delivers massive scale in highly parallelized environments. Multi-threaded synthetic stress testing achieves top-tier results with a stress-ng multi-core score of 313816.03, alongside top-tier memory bandwidth reaching 960.46 GB/s for large uncached reads and 483.72 GB/s for writes. Real-world parallel benchmarks demonstrate top-decile throughput, including 357.24 million Redis SET operations per second, a Geekbench Clang software compilation score of 84996.0, and 155.49 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-threaded metrics reflect moderate execution speeds, with single-core Geekbench and stress-ng scores settling in the middle 50% percentile.

Hardware cost efficiency is driven by high Graviton core density and a substantial 600 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. The primary tradeoff stems from the lack of integrated NVMe storage, meaning I/O-heavy operations must utilize remote EBS volumes over the network. With its balanced memory ratio, massive parallel compute capacity, and high network throughput, m8gn.48xlarge is suited for distributed in-memory caching tiers, large-scale software compilation pipelines, microservice web fleets, and parallel ETL batch processing.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gn.48xlarge is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by 192 dedicated physical ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 Graviton cores at 2.7 GHz and 768.0 GB of RAM. Operating under the Nitro system without hardware hyperthreading, the instance maintains a consistent 4.0 GB of memory per core alongside a 600 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. It contains no local NVMe storage and no GPUs, utilizing EBS volumes for disk operations. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier parallel compute throughput and memory bandwidth, demonstrated by 357.24 million Redis SET operations per second and elevated Geekbench Clang build scores, offset by moderate single-core speeds. The architectural configuration delivers balanced resource density and networking capability, making it well suited for large-scale in-memory key-value stores, distributed build systems, large web service backends, and parallelized data processing.
